I've known people from poor and rich schools, and never met anyone who did.

Seems like some sort of myth people invented.
Did you actually ever know anyone who lived on ramen or mac and cheese in college?
I did in elementary school being poor folk. You can make it pretty good by adding frozen veggies in the ramen, and chopped ham or canned meats in the mac n cheese.
I had stretches where that and a few other cheap foods (beans) were eaten pretty much every meal.

Did when I was a kid for lengthy stretches at a time. Throw some iceberg lettuce on the side of your veggies. Don't really have any complaints. I apparently got the nutrients I needed out of it so c'est la vie when you're broke. Put a can of beans in the mac for some variety and extra filling. Another good one is beans + rice + cornbread. Costs next to nothing, lasts forever, and it's pretty delicious too.

I didn't, because my school essentially forced us to buy a meal plan from them. It "wasn't required" to do so, but if you didn't you would lose 10% of the funding they gave you, which for most people came out to about the same cost as their meal plan. I fucking hated that place, and I feel bad for the poor sap who will call me begging for donations soon.

I had to, got foreclosed on a home, was living in a hotel and after all expenses I had $20 to feed myself every two weeks. Ramen was $14 for a case and could be made in a small crockpot in the hotel so that's what I ate, breakfast, lunch and dinner for 6 months.
What kind of a toll, physically, did that take on you?
I'm a grown man, living on my own, supporting myself. I currently live of pastas.

There's a period of time on one's young adulthood or independence, where you can make/eat whatever you want. In that era, making Ramen and/or mac & cheese is easy to make and cheap, which fits into the cooking skillset of most people in that era and works with the budget of those in that era.

Eventually, you learn to make other things that are better and can afford them, and you move on.

I knew plenty of Ramen/MacNCheese people in college and was somewhat of one myself (I made them occasionally, like 3-6 times a month, but never subsisted exclusively on them.)
